title: Diagonal tensor under an internal action-site presentation
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site with finite limits, K a sheaf of groups, R a commutative ring sheaf, and P a Presentation K J hJ R [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation]. For every two equivariant module sheaves M and N [def-sfb-equivariant-module-sheaves], their tensor corresponds under P to the base module sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with action a(x tensor y) = ax tensor ay. Both the underlying tensor identification and the action-site tensor identification commute with the actual sheafification images of pure tensors. Precisely, InternalDiagonalTensor J hJ K R P [def-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor-data] holds.

source.place: Tags 03D7, 03CY, 03DA and Section 03EK; internal-action application of steps 1--6 of lem-sfb-internal-restriction-module-tensor.

proof.text: For $K$-equivariant modules form the presheaf $P(U)=M(U)\otimes_{R(U)}N(U)$ and define $a(x\otimes y)=ax\otimes ay$. Linearity of each group operation makes this well defined on the balancing relations; its inverse is the operation of $a^{-1}$. Identity and composition follow on pure tensors, which generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Along $(f,a):V\to U$ in the action site the tensor restriction is therefore $x\otimes y\mapsto(a f^*x)\otimes(a f^*y)$. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] the action-site tensor is the module sheafification of exactly this presheaf. The sheafification assertion of [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] identifies its underlying sheaf with the base tensor sheaf and its action with the induced diagonal action. This also applies to $L$ and to trivial actions.

proof.text: The baseComparison and siteComparison of P commute with the respective sheafification units. Consequently the two induced tensor isomorphisms carry the displayed presheaf pure tensors to the specified sheaf pure tensors. These unit equations give both clauses of InternalDiagonalTensor, including the exact section map internalPresentationSection.
